theme: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

reports.title: Dorothy Imisson
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: No appropriate care plan was developed by the District Nursing Service
The District Nursing Service are compromising patient care by not following NMC guidance or record keeping
The District Nursing Services are compromising patient care by not following NICE guidelines

reports.title: Shannon Quinn
categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

concerns.quote: Evidence emerged during the inquest that there was inconsistent sharing of documentation and case notes between the statutory agencies and private sector. In particular, there was no sharing of medical notes/care plans between the Birmingham and Solihull and Mental Health Trust and Oak House
concerns.hazard: inconsistent sharing of medical notes and care plans between agencies

concerns.quote: There was inconsistent and minimal training provided to Oak House staff in respect of managing SQ's complex needs by the Mental Health Trust
concerns.hazard: inconsistent and minimal training for managing complex needs

concerns.quote: There was a lack of a joint multi-disciplinary/Trust care plan and insufficient contact with the care coordinator due to difficulties in travelling to meet the patient outside the normal Trust area and staff sickness absence
concerns.hazard: lack of joint multidisciplinary care plan and insufficient contact with care coordinator

concerns.quote: There was an escalating risk of use of ligatures and incidents of self-harm and little if any measures were introduced to try and provide a ligature free environment
concerns.hazard: escalating risk of ligature use and self-harm incidents

concerns.quote: The patient observation level of 5 minutes was introduced to minimise risk of self-harm but not adhered to
concerns.hazard: non-adherence to 5 minute observation for self-harm risk

concerns.quote: Evidence emerged during the inquest that there had been minimal training for Oak House staff in performing resuscitation on patients. The training received included general first aid training by e-learning
concerns.hazard: minimal training in resuscitation for Oak House staff

links.explanation: Both reports highlight failures in developing or sharing appropriate care plans leading to compromised patient care. The earlier focuses on district nursing service planning, while the later concerns joint multidisciplinary trust care planning and coordination.
links.earlier_quote: No appropriate care plan was developed by the District Nursing Service.
links.later_quote: There was a lack of a joint multi-disciplinary/Trust care plan and insufficient contact with the care coordinator due to difficulties in travelling to meet the patient outside the normal Trust area and staff sickness absence.
